subject: EdgeCase AI — trial scope, success gates & environment provisioning
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Moreno <alyssa.moreno@edgecase.ai>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@edgecase.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed focused trial

Hi Alyssa / Marcus —

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight trial approach so we can move to a scoped POC without burning a lot of cycles up front. TL;DR: we propose a 4-week, single-use-case trial (customer support triage) with clear success gates and a short access checklist.

Pain points you raised:
- High latency and unpredictable cost on current hosted classifiers leading to slow inference spikes during peak support traffic.
- Lack of visibility into per-route token economics for your routing rules.
- Need for deterministic failure modes (fallbacks) for SLA-sensitive channels.

Goals for the trial
- Reduce median token latency for triage flow by >= 40% under representative load.
- Demonstrate 30% lower per-conversation inference cost using batching + prefix caching.
- Validate rollout path for a VPC/private deployment if residency is required.

Proposed trial scope (4 weeks)
1) Week 0 (Prep, 3 business days): access & environment prep — Redwoods to provision a scoped project, service account, and sample prompt set.
2) Week 1–2 (Integration & tuning): connect a single triage route, ingest 10k dry-run examples, run prompt-evals to pin quality targets.
3) Week 3 (Load test & cost analysis): simulated peak traffic run, telemetry capture for cost/latency breakdowns.
4) Week 4 (Readout): review metrics, provide an adoption recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

Success gates (examples)
- Median token latency <= 120ms for triage endpoint at 95th percentile load profile.
- Fallback hit rate < 2% during simulated traffic spike.
- Evaluation score: intent-classification accuracy >= 88% vs baseline.

Owners / points of contact
- Redwood: Irene Choi (Eng + AM), Karthik Iyer (Solutions / integration), Ben Carter (Customer Success).
- EdgeCase: Alyssa Moreno (Product / trial owner), Marcus Li (Infra / security).

Immediate asks from our side
- Shared S3 or sample dataset (10k examples), or allow us to ingest anonymized subset (preferred).
- One infra contact with admin rights to create the service account (we’ll provide a narrow IAM template).
- Confirmation if the environment must be in the US-only region (vs. multi-region).

Attachments: edgecase_trial_scope.pdf (proposed scope + metrics), access_matrix.xlsx (minimal IAM + IP allowlist template).

Next steps
1) If this scope looks good, can we target a soft start date of Mon, Nov 23?
2) Alyssa / Marcus — please confirm dataset delivery timeline and residency requirement.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a mutual action plan link and a short access checklist.

Best,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

--
Attachment: edgecase_trial_scope.pdf (PDF, 312 KB)
Attachment: access_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 14 KB)

From: Alyssa Moreno <alyssa.moreno@edgecase.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@edgecase.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed focused trial

Thanks Irene — this is an excellent summary and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data & residency:
- We prefer US-only for the trial (EdgeCase handles customer PII). If Redwood can provide a US-only project, that’s preferred.

2) Dataset delivery:
- We can provide a sanitized 10k example set by Thu, Nov 20 (we will strip PII and provide a mapping doc). Our data engineer (Marcus) will share S3 write creds or a temporary presigned upload link.

3) Security ask:
- We will need a short security Q/A for our audit team (SOC 2 artifacts + network diagram). If you can attach the one-pager or a link that would speed our procurement.

4) Timeline
- Nov 23 start is fine. We have a product sprint deadline the following week; can we aim to keep Week 1 deliverables light (integration + sanity checks only)?

One additional concern: our current internal classifier sometimes misroutes short messages; we’d like the trial to include 1–2 prompts specifically for short-form utterances so the evals represent that distribution.

Happy to proceed once we have the S3 link and the US-region confirmation.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Moreno
Head of Product | EdgeCase AI

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed focused trial — kickoff plan + access checklist

Hi Alyssa / Marcus —

Great — glad Nov 23 works. A few concrete items from the engineering side to make Week 0 and Week 1 go smoothly. I’ve pasted a short kickoff checklist below and linked the mutual action plan.

Kickoff checklist (action owners & ETA)
- EdgeCase: provide sanitized sample dataset (10k) or presigned S3 upload — owner: Marcus — ETA: 2026-11-20 EOD.
- EdgeCase: confirm US-only residency requirement (reply to thread) — owner: Alyssa — ETA: 2026-11-19 EOD.
- Redwood: create trial project & service account; share key + restricted IAM role template — owner: Karthik — ETA: 2026-11-22.
- Redwood: upload initial prompt-set (includes short-form utterances) and run a 500-example prompt-eval — owner: Ben — ETA: 2026-11-24.
- Both: schedule 30-min tech sync during Week 1 (suggest Tue Nov 24 10:00–10:30 PST) — owner: Irene to set calendar hold.

Access matrix required
- We will need a single service account (programmatic) with a scoped role; if you prefer we can accept a temporary presigned S3 link instead (less privilege footprint). I attached an access_matrix.xlsx template with minimal fields we need (IAM role, IP allowlist, service account email).

Security artifacts for procurement
- Quick links: SOC 2 one-pager + network diagram: https://drive.redwood.example/security/soc2-onepager.pdf (we’ll also upload them to the mutual action plan). I’ll copy the SOC 2 executive summary into the MAP.

Mutual action plan & shared drive
- MAP: https://drive.redwood.example/edgecase/mutual-action-plan (contains timeline, owners, acceptance criteria).

Notes about runbook & success gating
- During Week 3 load test we’ll capture: 95th/99th token latency, fallbacks per-minute, and token cost per-conversation. We’ll publish a per-route dashboard so you can inspect token economics in real time.

Let me know if the Tue 11/24 sync conflicts with your sprint cadence — we can move it to Wed.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: access_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 14 KB)
Related links: https://drive.redwood.example/edgecase/mutual-action-plan

Also Marcus here (infra) — I can create the service account once you share the IAM template. Please send the service account email you want me to grant.

We’re good to start Nov 23 with a light Week 1 scope. I’ll join the Tue tech sync unless it moves.
